source_title: Politics News: Opposition's 'Jan Mahabhiyog' Programme Postponed Due to Rain, Now Scheduled for Tomorrow!
source_excerpt:
The Opposition's 'Jan Mahabhiyog' programme, which was scheduled to take place today, has been postponed due to continuous rainfall. According to sources, the Congress and INDIA bloc leaders will now organise the programme tomorrow in the same format as originally planned. The event was expected to bring together leaders from 21 opposition parties under the INDIA bloc to initiate an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and several other senior opposition leaders were scheduled to participate in the programme. Preparations for the event had reportedly been completed at the venue, with arrangements made for the gathering and the proposed proceedings. However, continuous rainfall since last night disrupted the preparations and affected the arrangements for the outdoor programme. As a result, the opposition decided to postpone the event rather than proceed with it under unfavourable weather conditions. According to information received from sources, the programme will now be held tomorrow, with the arrangements expected to remain largely the same as originally planned. The proposed initiative against Gyanesh Kumar was expected to begin with a motion to be introduced by Mallikarjun Kharge. Meanwhile, senior INDIA bloc leaders are expected to address a press conference at the venue to explain the reasons behind the postponement and share details about their next course of action. Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other prominent opposition leaders are expected to participate in the press conference. The postponement has added a new development to the opposition's planned political move against the Chief Election Commissioner. While the weather has disrupted today's schedule, the opposition is reportedly determined to go ahead with the programme tomorrow. The revised event and the statements from senior opposition leaders are now being closely watched.
